title: Composition, namespaced ids and scope:global ADR conflict surfacing
description: Multiple blueprints may be applied to a single project. Blueprint-contributed docs are namespaced by the blueprint's slug so ids cannot collide across blueprints. A blueprint's ADR contributions may be tagged `scope: global`; two applied blueprints each contributing a `scope: global` ADR are a genuine conflict and `rcf blueprint add` surfaces both entries and refuses to write. Conflict-presentation ergonomics are prototype-unknown #1 (design brief); this US covers the first pass.
iWant: blueprint contributions to compose without id collisions, and for `scope: global` ADR conflicts to be surfaced with both sides visible before anything is written
soThat: composition never silently merges incompatible whole-project decisions

acceptanceCriteria.description: Blueprint-contributed doc ids are namespaced with the blueprint's slug so composition cannot collide on ids at the id layer
acceptanceCriteria.given: two blueprints `spa` and `rest` that both contribute a REQ, a US and an ADR
acceptanceCriteria.when: both are applied to the same project via `rcf blueprint add`
acceptanceCriteria.then: every contributed id carries the blueprint slug as its prefix (REQ/US: `spa-REQ-001`, `rest-REQ-001`) or as its kebab-suffix (ADR: `ADR-004-spa-theme`, `ADR-005-rest-versioning`); no two contributed ids across the two blueprints match

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint add <slug>` refuses when the new blueprint contributes a `scope: global` ADR on a topic already contributed by an applied blueprint
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with blueprint `alpha` already applied contributing an ADR tagged `scope: global` on topic `versioning`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `rcf blueprint add beta` runs and blueprint `beta` also contributes a `scope: global` ADR on `versioning`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verb exits non-zero, prints both ADR ids and their file paths, and the manifest is unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.description: Conflict output leads with per-side headers (ADR title + one-sentence decision) and names four honest resolution paths with actual blueprint slugs filled in (Phase 3.5 reshape)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the output opens with `conflict on topic (<topic>)` and one line per side carrying `blueprint <slug>: <title> — <decision>` (or `<id> at <path>` when the tree did not carry the ADR body), a `refs:` footer with both ids + paths, and four honest resolutions numbered 1-4: adopt-incoming (`rcf blueprint remove <existing-slug>`), keep-existing (do not add the incoming), supersede via a project-level ADR (`rcf blueprint supersede <topic>`), and declare-on-add (`rcf blueprint add <source> --resolve <topic>=project:<ADR-id>`) — all with the actual conflicting blueprint slugs already substituted, no `<slug>` placeholders

acceptanceCriteria.description: Non-global TACs, ADRs, REQs, USs and FBSes are namespaced and cannot conflict
acceptanceCriteria.given: two blueprints each contributing a TAC on the same topic without `scope: global`
acceptanceCriteria.then: both TACs co-exist under distinct namespaced ids; no conflict is surfaced

acceptanceCriteria.description: Topic vocabulary is a lookup key, not a slug: `rcf blueprint supersede <topic>` and `rcf blueprint add --resolve <topic>=project:<ADR-id>` accept any topic that exact-matches an applied `scope:global` ADR's declared topic (the shipped SPA and REST blueprints use camelCase topics — authModel, errorEnvelope). The scaffolded project ADR id derives its slug tail by kebab-ifying the topic (`authModel` -> `ADR-NNN-auth-model`) so the ADR grammar's `[a-z0-9](-[a-z0-9]+)*` tail constraint is satisfied. Whitespace-only topics are refused at the writer edge (schema minLength: 1 does not reject whitespace). Following option 3 as printed by the reshaped conflict message against the shipped blueprints MUST be executable end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the shipped SPA + REST blueprints both applied on a project (both carry a scope:global ADR on the camelCase topic `authModel`)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs `rcf blueprint supersede authModel` as printed in option 3
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verb exits 0, scaffolds a project ADR at `rcf/adrs/adr-NNN-auth-model.json` (kebab-tailed adrId), records a `manifest.resolutions[]` entry with `topic: 'authModel'` (verbatim) and `resolvedByAdrId: 'ADR-NNN-auth-model'`, and both blueprint ADRs remain on disk as superseded history

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint add --reason <text>` attaches the operator's ruling text to every `manifest.resolutions[]` record minted on that add. Whitespace-only reasons are refused at the writer edge (schema does not enforce a minimum floor on the field itself; the writer's floor is emptiness, not length).
acceptanceCriteria.given: an incoming blueprint whose apply would collide on one or more topics, resolved via one or more --resolve declarations
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator adds `--reason "..."` alongside the --resolve flags
acceptanceCriteria.then: every newly-minted resolutions[] record carries the reason string verbatim; a whitespace-only --reason exits 2 with an error naming the topic and no record is written

acceptanceCriteria.description: Duplicate `--resolve` declarations for the same topic within a single `rcf blueprint add` are deduped: the first declaration is kept, subsequent declarations on the same topic are dropped, and a `[warn]` line names each dropped topic on stderr. The add still exits 0 on success; the manifest carries exactly one resolutions[] record per topic.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an incoming blueprint whose apply would collide on topic X
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator passes `--resolve X=project:ADR-A --resolve X=project:ADR-B` on the same command
acceptanceCriteria.then: the manifest carries exactly one resolutions[] record on topic X with `resolvedByAdrId: ADR-A` (first-wins), and stderr carries a warn line naming X as a duplicate --resolve topic

acceptanceCriteria.description: Conflict enrichment is symmetric: the CLI's conflict report and `--json` output both carry `title` + one-sentence `decision` on BOTH sides of a globalAdrTopic conflict — the existing side read from the walker's tree, the incoming side read from the blueprint's ADR file on disk. Round-1 only enriched the existing side, which read asymmetrically against shipped blueprints.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an incoming blueprint that would collide with an applied blueprint on a scope:global ADR topic, both ADRs carrying a title and a decision
acceptanceCriteria.when: `rcf blueprint add <source>` refuses with the reshaped message (with or without --json)
acceptanceCriteria.then: both `incoming` and `existing` sides render `blueprint <slug>: <title> — <decision>` in the terminal output, and `conflicts[].incoming` and `conflicts[].existing` both carry `title` and `decision` in the --json output
